record.paper_title: The Flow Associated to Weakly Differentiable Vector Fields: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Suppose the vector field has the singular-integral form b_t(x)=∫_{R^d} K(x-y)F_t(y)dy, where K is a standard singular-integral kernel. Can the corresponding well-posedness and flow theory be extended from the case F_t∈L^1(R^d)^d to the case where F_t is merely a measure? Such an extension would cover BV vector fields and even BD vector fields through the same elliptic-PDE representation argument discussed in the source.

evidence.quote: Recently Bouchut and Crippa achieved in [24] a very nice extension of the theory to vector fields bt that can be represented as a singular integral bt(x) = ∫Rd K(x − y)Ft(y) dy with Ft ∈ [L1(Rd)]d.

In this direction, it would be very nice to have an extension of this result to the case when Ft is just a measure, and not necessarily an L1 function. This would include BV and even BD vectorfields, by the same elliptic PDE argument illustrated above.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $d\ge 2$ and $T>0$. Consider a time-dependent vector field $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d$ of singular-integral form
$$b_t(x)=\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} K(x-y)\,dF_t(y),$$
where $K:\mathbb{R}^d\setminus\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is a standard Calderón–Zygmund singular-integral kernel (i.e. $K$ is smooth away from the origin, homogeneous of degree $-d$, has zero average on spheres centered at the origin, and the convolution operator $f\mapsto K*f$ is bounded on $L^p(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for $1<p<\infty$), and $F_t$ is, for almost every $t\in[0,T]$, a finite $\mathbb{R}^d$-valued Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $t\mapsto\|F_t\|_{\mathcal{M}}$ integrable on $[0,T]$. Assume in addition the usual growth bound on $b$ and the bound $\mathrm{div}\,b_t\in L^1((0,T);L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^d))$.

Question: Can the well-posedness and stability theory of the regular Lagrangian flow associated with the ODE $\dot{X}_t(x)=b_t(X_t(x))$, $X_0(x)=x$ — known when $F_t\in L^1(\mathbb{R}^d)^d$ — be extended to the case in which $F_t$ is allowed to be a (signed vector) Radon measure? Such an extension would in particular cover vector fields of bounded variation (BV) and of bounded deformation (BD), via the elliptic-PDE representation of $\nabla b$ (or its symmetric part) as a singular integral of a measure.
artifact.category_tag: Lagrangian flows for singular vector fields
artifact.status_search_result: The fully integrable case ($F_t\in L^1$) is the Bouchut–Crippa theorem. Subsequent work by Bohun–Bouchut–Crippa on Lagrangian flows with anisotropic regularity treats vector fields where some components have derivatives that are singular integrals of measures (motivated by Vlasov–Poisson with measure density), giving partial progress. Further work by Nguyen and others (including a 2025 paper on Lagrangian flows for very singular integral vector fields) advances the theory in specific singular kernel settings. A complete extension to general measure data $F_t$ covering arbitrary BV/BD vector fields does not appear to be available, so the problem is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian flows for vector fields with anisotropic regularity
status_evidence.snippet: Quantitative estimates for flows of vector fields subject to anisotropic regularity conditions: some derivatives of some components are (singular integrals of) measures, while the remaining derivatives are (singular integrals of) integrable functions.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress: the measure case is treated in anisotropic settings motivated by Vlasov–Poisson.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian flows for vector fields with gradient given by a singular integral
status_evidence.snippet: Bouchut–Crippa: existence, uniqueness, quantitative stability for flows when gradient is singular integral of an L^1 function.

status_evidence.title: Lagrangian Flow for Very Singular Integral Vector Fields and Application for Generalized SQG Equation
status_evidence.snippet: Existence, uniqueness and semigroup property for Lagrangian flows for vector fields defined as convolution with a non Calderón–Zygmund singular kernel.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2025) extensions of the theory in singular-kernel directions.
